clue.text: Trim a tree for Christmas

definitions.meaning: trim as an adjective means neat and smart in appearance
a conifer often brought indoors and decorated in December

explanation.surface: Instructions for decorating the festive tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trim' looks like a verb about decorating the tree; it is the adjective meaning neat.
explanation.definitionFit: Spruce means neat and tidy, like trim; the spruce is also the conifer traditionally used as the Christmas tree.

clue.text: Unusual individual

definitions.meaning: relating to one only, as in grammar's one-not-many form

explanation.definitionFit: Singular means remarkable or odd, and also single or one only, as opposed to plural.

clue.text: Swift's office when in the country?

definitions.text: Swift's office when in the country?

parts.words: Swift's office when in the country?
parts.note: Jonathan Swift held a church post as Dean of St Patrick's in Dublin; imagine that post in a rural setting

explanation.surface: A question about where the writer Swift worked when he left town.
explanation.walkthrough: Jonathan Swift, author of Gulliver's Travels, was a dean; a dean overseeing a group of country parishes has this title.
explanation.definitionFit: The clerical post responsible for a deanery of rural parishes in the Church of England.

clue.text: Cleaner way to make carbon

definitions.meaning: a British word for a woman hired to clean houses
burning something partly reduces it to blackened carbon

explanation.surface: A tip about a cleaner method for producing carbon.
explanation.walkthrough: A char (charwoman) is a British cleaning lady; to char is to scorch something black.
explanation.definitionFit: A char is a domestic cleaner in British usage, and charring is scorching a substance until it turns to charcoal.

clue.text: See 12
Prepare to sail — endless task on superior vessel

indicators.note: on joins the pieces, the task coming after the other two

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for upper-class, socially superior
a pan is a cooking vessel

indicators.note: endless says the final letter of the word for task is dropped

parts.note: a chore is a routine task

explanation.surface: A sailor told to get ready while doing a never-ending job aboard a fine ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the last letter of CHORE to give CHOR. U for upper-class is a British convention.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise the anchor is the step a ship takes before setting off on a voyage.

clue.text: Device for torturing Tom's gang

parts.note: Tom Thumb is the tiny hero of an English folk tale, so Tom's leads to his surname plus the possessive S
a crew is a gang or band of people

explanation.surface: A torture device belonging to a certain Tom's gang.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Thumb is the thumb-sized boy of English folklore, so 'Tom's gang' is Thumb's crew.
explanation.definitionFit: An old instrument of torture that crushed the victim's fingers in a vice.

clue.text: Method said to obtain a windfall

indicators.note: said tells us to take the word as heard, not as written

parts.note: a manner is a way or method of doing something

explanation.surface: A recommended technique for getting a lucky gain.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech MANNER and MANNA sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Manna was food falling from heaven in the Bible, so it means any unexpected godsend.

clue.text: Desire to be broadcast live

indicators.note: broadcast also means scattered widely, so the letters of the word desire are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone yearning to appear on air in real time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'live' reads as in a live broadcast; it is the verb meaning dwell.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside somewhere is to dwell there permanently.

clue.text: Bird-dog, not black

indicators.note: not says the letter for black is to be left out

parts.note: a beagle is a breed of hound
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A bird-dog that isn't black.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird-dog' looks like a gun dog, but the hyphen hides a split: 'Bird' is the definition and 'dog' the start of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A large bird of prey, the golden one being the best known.

clue.text: Frontline caught in seething rain -its heavenly!

definitions.note: read as it's heavenly, a description of a blissful state rather than an adjective alone

indicators.note: caught in says one piece is held inside the other
seething means churning, so the letters of rain are stirred up

parts.note: the van, short for vanguard, is the front line of an army

explanation.surface: Someone at the front, caught in pouring rain, oddly finds it blissful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frontline' looks like a military adjective; the van (vanguard) is the front of an army. The print drops the apostrophe of 'it's', the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In Buddhism this is the state of perfect bliss and release, so the word means any paradise.

clue.text: Old boy found in compound with students

parts.note: alum is a chemical compound, a double sulphate
NUS is the National Union of Students in Britain

explanation.surface: An old boy discovered in a fenced compound alongside students.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compound' suggests an enclosure; it is a chemical one. The NUS is the British students' union body.
explanation.definitionFit: A former pupil or graduate of a school or college, a male one in Latin form.

clue.text: Dangerous antagonist who'd challenge a beautician

definitions.meaning: someone so plain-faced a beauty therapist would struggle, a playful reading

explanation.surface: A tough opponent for someone who does makeovers.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a menacing person to deal with; taken literally, an unattractive client would test a beauty therapist.

clue.text: Gloomy trustees provide outdated aid for teachers

parts.note: black means dismal or gloomy, as in a black mood
a board of trustees governs a body

explanation.surface: Downbeat trustees supply an old-fashioned teaching aid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provide' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The chalk-written board once fixed at the front of every classroom, now replaced by whiteboards.

clue.text: Exciting book features Buttons, a famous artist

parts.note: Buttons is the page in the British Cinderella pantomime, and a page boy's uniform has rows of buttons
J. M. W. Turner was the celebrated English landscape painter

explanation.surface: A thrilling book featuring Buttons and a great painter.
explanation.walkthrough: In British pantomime, Buttons is Cinderella's friend, a page boy; Turner is the English painter of seascapes.
explanation.definitionFit: A gripping read that keeps you flicking on to the next leaf.

clue.text: A chap takes exercise like Tarzan

definitions.note: a noun sense, someone of Tarzan's kind

indicators.note: takes means the other pieces hold the exercise letters inside them

parts.note: a chap is a man
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: A man doing a workout to look like Tarzan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like Tarzan' stands for a noun: the kind of jungle-raised man Tarzan was.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarzan, raised in the jungle by great apes, is the classic wild man brought up among primates.

clue.text: Business worry

explanation.definitionFit: A going concern is a company, and concern is also anxiety about something.

clue.text: With which Caesar scented conspiracy, perhaps

definitions.text: With which Caesar scented conspiracy, perhaps

parts.words: With which Caesar scented conspiracy, perhaps
parts.note: pictures the emperor sniffing out the plot against him with his distinctive aquiline organ

explanation.surface: Julius Caesar sensing the plot against him.
explanation.walkthrough: To smell a rat is to sense a plot; a Roman's nose is also a term for a high-bridged nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A nose with a prominent curved bridge, as seen on Roman statues and coins.

clue.text: Coolness — it's unlikely in a disco

definitions.meaning: dancers on a crowded floor are packed close together, so space between people is rare

explanation.surface: Aloofness won't last on a packed dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping one's distance means being reserved, and physical separation is scarce in a crowded nightclub.

clue.text: Where skilful potter should get richer

definitions.text: Where skilful potter should get richer

parts.words: Where skilful potter should get richer
parts.note: a snooker player pots balls into a table's pouch, and the phrase also means having money

explanation.surface: A good ceramicist should prosper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potter' suggests a ceramicist, but here a snooker player who pots balls; the phrase also means financially ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: A potted ball ends in the table's pocket, and the phrase also means having made a profit.

clue.text: Have some assets left

parts.note: read as receiving property bequeathed in a will, not as having savings remaining

explanation.surface: Someone checking whether there's money still in the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' suggests remaining; here it means bequeathed after a death.
explanation.definitionFit: To receive property or money from someone who has died, as heir.

clue.text: European who's related, almost

indicators.note: almost means the word stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: germane means relevant or related

explanation.surface: A continental who is nearly a relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'who's' is a link; 'related' suggests family, but means relevant.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Germany, a country of Europe.

clue.text: Assist in motion or its opposite

definitions.note: the opposite of motion, a noun phrase

indicators.note: in motion means the letters of assist are moved around

explanation.surface: Help either moving or standing still.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in motion' is both anagram signal and the word whose opposite is defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Stasis is a state of standstill or equilibrium, the reverse of movement.

clue.text: Leak from a lighter

definitions.meaning: an accidental escape of liquid, a slop
a thin strip of wood or twisted paper used to light a fire or pipe

explanation.surface: Fluid escaping from a cigarette lighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lighter' suggests a gas lighter; here it is something you use to light a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A spill is liquid that has leaked out, and also a taper of wood or paper for lighting fires.

clue.text: Variety of toilet roll? Possibly vital for a surgeon!

definitions.meaning: a playful reading: a kind of loo paper, as tissue is soft paper
the biological matching of donor and recipient cells needed in transplants

explanation.surface: A loo-roll brand that a surgeon cannot do without.
explanation.definitionFit: Tissue typing matches organs between donor and patient; humorously, a kind of soft paper.

clue.text: Second man on board to give birth

parts.note: a pawn is a chess piece, and chessmen are called men

explanation.surface: A deputy on the ship's board brought in to deliver a baby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man on board' suggests a sailor; it is a piece on a chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish and frogs spawn when they lay masses of eggs, producing offspring.

clue.text: Defeat in round one

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Losing in the opening round of a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round one' looks like boxing, but it simply holds the letters across the word break.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring about someone's ruin or downfall.

clue.text: One of those giants of progress

indicators.note: of says the answer is a part taken out of the next word

explanation.surface: A figure who is one of the great movers of advancement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giants of progress' looks like a phrase about pioneers; the giant is inside 'progress'.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-eating giant of fairy tales.

clue.text: Quiet girl on the river

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
Ann is a girl's name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A quiet girl standing by the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Shannon is Ireland's longest river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shannon is the longest river in Ireland.

clue.text: Record of fire wood by volume

parts.note: a log is a piece of wood for burning
a volume is a book

explanation.surface: A record of firewood measured by volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link; 'volume' looks like quantity but is a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's or vehicle's official written record of journeys and details.

clue.text: Odds and ends a newspaper preserves

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
to dry food preserves it, so preserves gives dries

explanation.surface: A paper keeps miscellaneous bits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'preserves' looks like jam; it is a verb, dries. The Sun is a British tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: Sundries are miscellaneous small items, bits and pieces.

clue.text: Deprived of beer, sadly, and your paper

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters of beer are jumbled

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times, the paper the solver is reading

explanation.surface: Left without beer, and without the paper too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' turns BEER into BERE; 'your paper' is the Financial Times, where this puzzle appears.
explanation.definitionFit: Bereft means having lost or lacking something, robbed of it.
